title: Port of the Moon
description: A short film on Bordeaux’s World Heritage listing, named for the crescent-shaped bend of the Garonne. Its riverfront of stone facades was built mostly in the 1700s. The Pont de Pierre, finished in 1822, was the first bridge across.

title: The battle that ended English Bordeaux
episode: Battle of Castillon, 1453 ⚔️ The end of the Hundred Years' War
description: An animated account of Castillon, east of Bordeaux, where French cannon destroyed an English army in July 1453. Bordeaux, English since 1154, surrendered that October, ending the Hundred Years’ War.

title: Remembering the slave trade
episode: Slave trade: the difficult work of memory in Bordeaux
description: A short report on how Bordeaux faces its past as France’s second-largest slave-trading port, which sent hundreds of ships to Africa in the 1700s. The Musée d’Aquitaine opened galleries on the trade in 2009.

title: Left Bank and Right Bank
episode: The Wines of Bordeaux's Right Bank
description: An introduction to the Right Bank, the vineyards east of the Dordogne around Saint-Émilion and Pomerol, where merlot rules. Saint-Émilion’s church was carved out of the limestone hill in the 1100s.

title: Canelés
description: How to make a canelé, the small fluted cake of Bordeaux, with a dark caramelized crust and a soft custard center flavored with rum and vanilla. Bakeries along Rue Sainte-Catherine sell them by the box.
